summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his study of al-Wajiz fi Kitab al-Salah, focusing on the prerequisites and conditions of prayer. He explains that salah is obligatory upon every Muslim who meets three essential conditions: being Muslim, having reached the age of puberty, and being sane. Sh. Ali Mashhour details the signs of puberty (pubic hair, age 15, sexual maturity, and menstruation for girls) and explains that at puberty, angels begin recording both good and bad deeds. He then provides an in-depth discussion on sanity in Islamic law, defining it as the ability to hold coherent intentions, and distinguishes between insanity and stupidity by explaining that insanity involves incoherent goals pursued coherently, while stupidity involves coherent goals pursued incoherently.
